ROUTE_IDENTITY.measured: production-field-map.json routeKeys is exactly the single MASTER_QUEUE route key, obligation:track-pathway:LA:la-976-arrest-no-conviction:non-conviction-arrest-expungement. The identity is on the delivered page, not only in metadata: page 1 prints 'ARTICLE 989 MOTION FOR EXPUNGEMENT OF A RECORD OF ARREST THAT DID NOT RESULT IN A CONVICTION, UNDER ARTICLE 976' and Part II recites Article 976(A) by its own terms. Louisiana runs six tracks off six articles that share the Article 989/991/992 instruments, and the packet disambiguates itself on its own face: 'Whether any charge on this arrest ended in a misdemeanour or felony conviction: No', with the printed statement that a conviction on this arrest puts the matter in Article 977 or Article 978 and means this is the wrong packet. The guide's opening section names all six sibling tracks and which article each is.

I measured against the bytes. Both declared digests were recomputed here with sha256sum at the declared paths in the mounted private custody and both match exactly: LA-CCRP-ART-993 = 0e455d3decea4b9e6299e1d39ceeb2b19ddaad93de19b2faa38d311f2d989ea2 and LA-CCRP-ART-990 = 13396bb180962be61788f0f7dd965fe4095d2262506b097623a86a6268e7a65a. The nested class is contradicted by measurement. Neither of those two is rendered into the packet and rendered-artifacts.json says so (renderedIntoThePacket false on both), which is correct: Article 990 is the responding agency's own affidavit and Article 993 is the withheld continuation sheet. The four instruments this packet does render carry no binary at all and are not claimed to; they are composed under the LA-STATUTORY-FORMS owner determination, read first hand, which grants this familyId exactly LA-CCRP-ART-988, 989, 991 and 992 and lists remainOfficialAndMustBeHeld as empty. Every pageManifest entry accordingly carries sourceSha256 null with sourceClass composed_from_the_committed_statutory_authority, which is an honest declaration rather than a missing digest.

ROUTE_OPTIONS.measured: The route fixes the article; the case fixes the ground. The Article 976(A) ground election prints as an empty two-line dot leader on the motion and again on the Article 992 order, with the printed reason that the ground is established by the minute entry and the district attorney's certification and that Louisiana State Police names choosing the wrong eligibility basis as a common fatal error. That is a refusal to guess a legal conclusion, not a missing option. The one election the packet does make for the participant, that no charge on this arrest ended in a conviction, is stated affirmatively on the face with the routing consequence printed beside it rather than left as a silent blank. No option list was mis-ordered because there is no AcroForm and no widget option list in this file.

REPEATING_ROWS.measured: This family delivers no repeating row structure. The Article 989 form carries single-instance charge lines and a 'How many separate charges or counts this arrest carries' line, not a numbered charge grid, and the multi-count case is routed off this packet to the withheld Article 993 continuation sheet. There is no AcroForm in either fixture, so the acroform-index-is-not-the-printed-row defect has no surface here: there are no widget indices to disagree with a printed row number. Recorded as not measurable rather than as a pass, because there is nothing of this kind to measure.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.measured: The fee law is stated correctly and the waiver instrument is correctly delivered and correctly left unsigned. The failure is what else is printed on the waiver instrument. Canonical page 7, on the face of the Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption, between the form's own instruction and the participant's identifying fields, prints a paragraph headed 'Why this component is in this packet:' which then recites the build record's own generation condition verbatim in quotation marks - 'Generated wherever the participant may qualify for the Article 983(F) exemption, which on this track is common.' - and goes on to cite three internal build records by name: 'The committed fee rule states that the exemption is very often available on this track and must be screened before filing rather than after, and the committed legal-design record directs that every participant on this track is routed through Article 988 before filing.' None of that is statute text or rule text. It is the builder's justification for including the component, addressed to a reviewer, and the quoted sentence is an instruction written to tell a builder when to generate a component. It is printed on a document that page 8 directs the participant to take or send to the district attorney's office before filing and to append to the motion at filing. This is the defect class the Captain recorded as internal-record-text-printed-on-a-filing at data/rcap-grade-a/packet-factory-24h/DEFECTS_NO_COUNTER_CAN_SEE.json, whose stated rule is 'Filings recite statute citations and rule text only. The record's own words belong in the guide, labelled as internal record text', and whose foundBy names this family. It is not a corpus convention: the phrase 'Why this component is in this packet' was searched across all seventeen canonical.pdf fixtures materialised in this checkout across LA, HI and OR and occurs in exactly one, this one. The packet also argues against itself here - page 1 of its own Article 989 motion prints that Article 986 provides only the statutory forms shall be used, with no local variant, and that Article 986(C) lets a clerk alter the form only to show the name of the court. No counter sees this: the text is present, non-empty, inside its write box and quoted accurately from a controlling record, so every gate passes. Two of the three things PF14 was recorded as finding are genuinely gone from the delivered bytes - there is no machine vocabulary of eligible dispositions printed as a bullet list, the Article 976(A) grounds being recited as statutory prose, and no memo component note at the foot of any composed form, checked page by page - but this third instance survives on the delivered page.
